```html
}

/* ---------- SVG drawing ---------- */
.n { cursor: default; }
.live .n[data-id], .live .e[data-id], .live .part[data-id] { cursor: pointer; }
.n .box { fill: var(--surface); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1.5; }
.n .halo { fill: none; stroke: transparent; stroke-width: 9; }
.n.touched .halo { stroke: var(--lamp-glow); }
.n.selected .halo { stroke: var(--lamp); stroke-width: 5; }
.c-proposed .box { fill: var(--ok-soft); stroke: var(--ok); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.c-sketch .box { fill: var(--bg); stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-dasharray: 1.5 5; stroke-linecap: round; }
.c-missing .box { fill: var(--dead-soft); stroke: var(--dead); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.c-checking .box { fill: var(--ai-soft); stroke: var(--ai); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; animation: march 1s linear infinite; }
.k-job .box, .k-external .box { stroke-dasharray: 7 4; }
.nm { font: 600 14px var(--font); fill: var(--ink); }
.sb { font: 400 11px var(--mono); fill: var(--muted); }
.hd { font: 500 11px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); }
.fl { font: 600 11px var(--font); text-anchor: end; fill: var(--muted); }
.c-code .fl { fill: var(--ok); } .c-proposed .fl { fill: var(--ok); } .c-missing .fl { fill: var(--dead); } .c-checking .fl { fill: var(--ai); }
.e path { fill: none; stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-width: 1.5; }
.e .hit { stroke: transparent; stroke-width: 14; }
.e-proposed path.ln { stroke: var(--ok); stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.e-missing path.ln { stroke: var(--dead); stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.e-checking path.ln { stroke: var(--ai); stroke-width: 2; stroke-dasharray: 6 5; animation: march 1s linear infinite; }
.e-sketch path.ln { stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-dasharray: 1.5 5; stroke-linecap: round; }
.e-behind path.ln { stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-dasharray: 2 5; }
.e.selected path.ln { stroke-width: 3; }
.lb { font: 500 11.5px var(--font); fill: var(--ink); text-anchor: middle; }
.e-proposed .lb { fill: var(--ok); } .e-missing .lb { fill: var(--dead); } .e-checking .lb { fill: var(--ai); }
.lbg { fill: var(--bg); stroke: none; }
.area { fill: var(--surface); fill-opacity: .45; stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-width: 1; }
.area-t { font: 600 12.5px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); }
.lane { fill: var(--surface); fill-opacity: .4; stroke: var(--line); }
.lane.alt { fill-opacity: .15; }
.lane-t { font: 600 12.5px var(--font-display); fill: var(--ink); }
.scr .scr-box { fill: var(--surface); stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1.5; }
.scr.c-missing .scr-box { fill: var(--dead-soft); stroke: var(--dead); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.scr-t { font: 600 13.5px var(--font-display); fill: var(--ink); }
.scr-r { font: 400 10.5px var(--mono); fill: var(--muted); }
.w-bar { fill: var(--line); }
.w-card { fill: none; stroke: var(--line); }
.w-card-t { font: 600 12px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); }
.w-tx { font: 400 12px var(--font); fill: var(--ink); }
.w-btn rect { fill: var(--ink); } .w-btn text { font: 600 11px var(--font); fill: var(--bg); text-anchor: middle; }
.w-tag rect { fill: var(--ok-soft); stroke: var(--ok); } .w-tag text { font: 600 11px var(--font); fill: var(--ok); text-anchor: middle; }
.w-kpi rect { fill: var(--bg); stroke: var(--line-strong); } .w-kpi .v { font: 700 28px var(--font-display); fill: var(--ink); } .w-kpi .l { font: 400 11.5px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); }
.part.selected rect { stroke: var(--lamp); stroke-width: 4; }
.note-box { fill: var(--surface); stroke: var(--line); }
.note-t { font: 400 12.5px var(--font); fill: var(--ink); }
.note-t.s { font: 500 11.5px var(--mono); fill: var(--muted); }
.life { stroke: var(--line-strong); stroke-dasharray: 3 5; }
.msg { stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; }
.msg.miss { stroke: var(--dead); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; stroke-width: 2; }
@keyframes march { to { stroke-dashoffset: -22; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .c-checking .box, .e-checking path.ln { animation: none; } }

/* ---------- the spec ---------- */
main { max-width: 1320px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px 24px 72px; display: grid; gap: 52px; }
section { display: grid; gap: 14px; }
h2 { margin: 0; font: 700 clamp(22px, 2.3vw, 28px)/1.15 var(--font-display); letter-spacing: -.01em; text-wrap: balance; }
h3 { margin: 0; font: 600 16px/1.25 var(--font-display); }
.prose { max-width: 68ch; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.prose p { margin: 0; }
.tight { margin: 0; padding-left: 18px; display: grid; gap: 5px; max-width: 72ch; }
figure { margin: 0; display: grid; gap: 8px; }
figcaption { font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--muted); max-width: 80ch; }
.fig { overflow-x: auto; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; padding: 14px; color: var(--ink); }
.fig svg { display: block; min-width: 780px; width: 100%; height: auto; }
.fb { fill: var(--surface); stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.4; }
.fb.hi { fill: var(--lamp-soft); stroke: var(--lamp); stroke-width: 2; }
.fb.ai { fill: var(--ai-soft); stroke: var(--ai); }
.fb.ok { fill: var(--ok-soft); stroke: var(--ok); }
.fc { fill: none; stroke: var(--line-strong); }
.ft { font: 600 13px var(--font); fill: currentColor; text-anchor: middle; }
.fs { font: 400 11px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); text-anchor: middle; }
.fm { font: 400 11px var(--mono); fill: var(--muted); text-anchor: middle; }
.fl2 { font: 500 11.5px var(--font); fill: currentColor; text-anchor: middle; }
.fh { font: 600 12.5px var(--font); fill: var(--muted); }
.fa { fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.4; }
.fa.back { stroke: var(--dead); stroke-dasharray: 6 5; }
.tablewrap { overflow-x: auto; }
table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; min-width: 720px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden; font-size: 14px; }
th, td { text-align: left; vertical-align: top; padding: 9px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
th { font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted); }
tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 0; }
td code { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.claims { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; }
.claim { background: var(--surface); border: 1.5px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 14px; padding: 13px 15px; display: grid; gap: 4px; align-content: start; }
.claim.p { border: 1.5px dashed var(--ok); background: var(--ok-soft); }
.claim.s { border: 1.5px dotted var(--line-strong); background: transparent; }
.claim p { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; }
.claim small { color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; }
.gallery { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(100%, 400px), 1fr)); gap: 14px; }
.card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.card .thumb { background-color: var(--bg); background-image: radial-gradient(var(--dot) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 12px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
.card .thumb svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; }
.card .txt { padding: 11px 14px 13px; display: grid; gap: 5px; font-size: 13.5px; flex: 1; align-content: start; }
.card .txt p { margin: 0; }
.card .txt .lab { color: var(--muted); }
.card .open { justify-self: start; margin-top: 3px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong); background: transparent; border-radius: 999px; padding: 3px 11px; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; }
pre.code { margin: 0; font: 12.5px/1.6 var(--mono); background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 14px; overflow-x: auto; }
pre.code .p { color: var(--ok); } pre.code .a { color: var(--ai); } pre.code .x { color: var(--dead); } pre.code .c { color: var(--muted); }
.two { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 420px), 1fr)); gap: 14px; align-items: start; }
.two > div { display: grid; gap: 8px; min-width: 0; }
.tag-t { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; }
.callout { background: var(--lamp-soft); border-left: 3px solid var(--lamp); border-radius: 8px; padding: 11px 14px; max-width: 80ch; display: grid; gap: 5px; }
.callout p { margin: 0; }
</style>
</head>
<body>

<header class="intro">
  <div class="brand"><i></i>illuminate</div>
  <h1>Claude explains with pictures, and every picture shows what's real</h1>
  <p>A design for the full build: illuminate becomes the place you work with Claude on your code. Claude answers in short sentences and live visuals, and each part of a visual says whether it's in the code, proposed or just a sketch. Try the working prototype below, then read how it gets built.</p>
</header>

<div class="frame">
  <div class="app live" id="app">
    <div class="bar">
      <span class="logo"><i></i>illuminate</span>
      <span class="where">care-app · Claude Code on your own sign-in</span>
      <span class="trust" id="trust" aria-live="polite"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="body">
      <div class="chat">
        <div class="log" id="log" aria-live="polite"></div>
        <div class="detail" id="detail" hidden></div>
        <form class="composer" id="composer">
          <input id="q" aria-label="Message to Claude" autocomplete="off">
          <button class="btn" type="submit">Send</button>
        </form>
      </div>
      <div class="stage">
        <div class="tabs" id="tabs" role="group" aria-label="Visuals in this session"></div>
        <div class="vis-title" id="vtitle"></div>
        <div class="canvas" id="canvas"></div>
        <div class="legend">
          <span><i></i>In the code</span>
          <span><i class="p"></i>Proposed</span>
          <span><i class="s"></i>Sketch</span>
          <span><i class="m"></i>Missing</span>
          <span><i class="c"></i>Being checked</span>
          <span><i class="t"></i>This change touches it</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="proto-note">Prototype with scripted replies, built on illuminate's care-app example. Press Send to play the next turn, click any box, arrow or screen control to point at it, and on the Wired screen press a control to see what's behind it. Nothing here calls Claude.</p>
</div>

<main>

<section>
  <h2>What changes</h2>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Today illuminate is something you call: ask a question, wait for a map, read it. In this design it's where the conversation happens. Claude has one new way to speak, a tool that draws, and uses it whenever a picture would say it faster than a paragraph.</p>
    <p>The checker stays, and its job gets wider. It used to decide whether a part could appear. Now anything can appear, and the checker decides how it looks. A hypothetical diagram is honest because it's drawn as hypothetical, right next to the parts that are proven.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="claims">
  <h2>Every part of a visual is one of three things</h2>
  <div class="claims">
    <div class="claim">
      <h3>In the code</h3>
      <p>Passed <code>check()</code> against the repo, and rechecked every time it opens.</p>
      <small>Solid ink. This is every part of today's maps.</small>
    </div>
    <div class="claim p">
      <h3>Proposed</h3>
      <p>Doesn't exist yet. What it connects to and touches is checked, so the plan sits on real ground. It turns solid once the code exists.</p>
      <small>Green and dashed, like today's fix arrow.</small>
    </div>
    <div class="claim s">
      <h3>Sketch</h3>
      <p>An idea with no claim about the code, for concepts and early thinking. Never counted in "matches the code".</p>
      <small>Dotted and unfilled. It's what you get unless Claude marks a part otherwise.</small>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Two states sit on top of these. <b>Missing</b> is today's absence claim, proven by a search and drawn in red. <b>Being checked</b> is a violet dashed part that claims to be in the code and hasn't been confirmed yet. If the check fails, the part gets flagged on the canvas and Claude is told, so it can correct itself in the same turn.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="visuals">
  <h2>Ten kinds of visual, one format</h2>
  <div class="prose"><p>They all share one format and one checker. Each kind adds a layout and the rule for when Claude reaches for it. The small pictures are the prototype's own renderer, and the button opens each one at full size above.</p></div>
  <div class="gallery" id="gallery"></div>
</section>

<section id="features">
  <h2>Features, and who asked for them</h2>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table>
    <thead><tr><th style="width:22%">Feature</th><th>What it does</th><th style="width:30%">Where it came from</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><b>Short replies plus a visual</b></td><td>Claude says two or three sentences, and the picture carries the rest. A chip in the reply reopens that visual.</td><td>Dhruv: "a block of text rather than just showing the workflow"</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Point and ask</b></td><td>Click a box, arrow, screen control or region, and your next message is about it. This exists today, and now reaches any session question.</td><td>Your own interface feedback (<code>HANDOFF.md</code> section 4)</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Point and change</b></td><td>"Remove this connection" with a box selected redraws the plan, then edits the code once you approve.</td><td>Patrick told an agent to remove a GitHub connection from a dependency graph</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>What this would touch</b></td><td>Worked out from code facts with no model: callers, imports and routes around the change light up in lamp yellow.</td><td>Dhruv has to understand the system before making a client's change</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Options side by side</b></td><td>Two or three proposals drawn on the same real parts, each with the files it touches. You pick by pointing.</td><td>Jay compares mockups side by side and chooses</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Press the screen, see the wiring</b></td><td>A rough wireframe of a real page. Press a control or KPI and its route, queries and tables appear beside it.</td><td>Dhruv's dashboard and "how was this KPI sourced?"</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Journeys by person</b></td><td>Screens as cards in a lane per person, moves as labelled arrows, the backend in a strip beneath. Pages grouped by what they touch.</td><td>Pat's user flows and design bible, Aditya's journey idea</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Watch it build</b></td><td>The approved plan stays on the canvas while Claude works. Parts turn violet as they're edited and solid when they pass the check.</td><td>Pat let an agent run for an hour and got the wrong thing</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Approve in the page</b></td><td>Claude Code's permission prompts arrive in the conversation with the exact diff. Allow, deny or send a correction.</td><td>Dhruv stays in the loop by choice, Patrick finds staying in the loop tiring</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Keep and share</b></td><td>Visuals save to <code>.illuminate/</code> with the conversation. Export one as a single HTML page for a cofounder or client, with its check date on it.</td><td>Abel: send a diagram to someone less technical. Jay's technical cofounder</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Stale marker</b></td><td>When the code moves, a reopened visual rechecks itself and says which parts no longer match.</td><td>Already built for maps, carried over</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Move to the terminal and back</b></td><td>The same conversation can reopen with <code>claude --resume</code>, so nobody is locked into the page.</td><td>Shonn's doubt about the medium; people keep their tools</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table></div>
</section>

<section id="speed">
  <h2>How a picture appears quickly</h2>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Most of a map's cost is citations and written explanation. In the saved map for "how does the agent develop visualisations", the whole thing is 11,100 characters. The boxes and arrows alone, written compactly, take about 1,100, which I estimate at roughly 350 tokens. So the main session writes only that short form and the picture appears at once. Checking then catches up in the background.</p>
  </div>
  <figure>
    <div class="fig">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 1040 372" role="img" aria-label="The main session sends a short sketch that is laid out and shown immediately. A facts pass and then a cheap read-only Claude prove parts through check, which turns them solid. Anything that fails goes back to the main session.">
        <defs><marker id="fa1" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker>
        <marker id="fa1r" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" style="fill:var(--dead)"/></marker></defs>
        <rect class="fb" x="30" y="40" width="190" height="70" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="125" y="70">Main session</text><text class="fs" x="125" y="90">already has the context</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="310" y="40" width="190" height="70" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="405" y="70">Parse and lay out</text><text class="fs" x="405" y="90">on your machine, no model</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="310" y="150" width="190" height="70" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="405" y="180">Facts pass</text><text class="fs" x="405" y="200">symbols, calls, imports, no model</text>
        <rect class="fb ai" x="310" y="260" width="190" height="70" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="405" y="290">Grounder</text><text class="fs" x="405" y="310">cheap Claude, read-only tools</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="590" y="150" width="170" height="70" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="675" y="180">check()</text><text class="fs" x="675" y="200">the same one, unchanged rule</text>
        <rect class="fb hi" x="850" y="40" width="160" height="290" rx="12"/><text class="ft" x="930" y="172">Canvas</text><text class="fs" x="930" y="192">dashed first,</text><text class="fs" x="930" y="208">solid as parts pass</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M220,75 H310" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="265" y="64">show (~350 tokens)</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M500,75 H850" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="675" y="64">drawn at once</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M405,110 V150" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="470" y="134">each claim</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M405,220 V260" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="480" y="244">what facts can't prove</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M500,185 H590" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="545" y="176">proven</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M500,295 C560,295 600,270 640,220" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="590" y="262">citations</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M760,185 H850" marker-end="url(#fa1)"/><text class="fl2" x="805" y="176">status</text>
        <path class="fa back" d="M700,220 V356 H125 V110" marker-end="url(#fa1r)"/><text class="fl2" x="410" y="350" style="fill:var(--dead)">what failed goes back, and Claude corrects it</text>
      </svg>
    </div>
    <figcaption>The main session never writes citations. Parts that name a real function can go solid from code facts alone. The grounder handles what's left, and its mistakes can't reach the screen because <code>check()</code> still decides.</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table>
    <thead><tr><th>Stage</th><th>Who does it</th><th>Tokens</th><th>Target, none measured yet</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>Sketch on screen</td><td>Main session writes it, then layout runs locally</td><td>About 350 on the main session</td><td class="tag-t">Under 5 s from Claude deciding to draw</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Named parts confirmed</td><td>Facts pass and <code>check()</code>, no model</td><td>None</td><td class="tag-t">Under 1 s after the sketch</td></tr>
      <tr><td>The rest confirmed</td><td>Grounder on a cheap model</td><td>Its own, kept out of the main thread</td><td class="tag-t">Under 30 s</td></tr>
      <tr><td>A full map, as today</td><td>Grounder, adding explanations and a walkthrough</td><td>Its own</td><td class="tag-t">Only on request</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table></div>
  <div class="prose">
    <p><b>When Claude draws.</b> The tool description says to draw when three or more things connect, when a change touches more than one file, when comparing options, or when you ask. Otherwise it answers in words. This gets tuned with the routing test already planned in <code>HANDOFF.md</code>: 10 to 15 real questions, each with the expected behaviour.</p>
    <p><b>Tokens.</b> A sketch costs about as much as the two paragraphs it replaces, so savings depend on Claude staying brief and people re-asking less. The tool's reply reminds Claude that the person can see the picture. The product should log tokens per session from day one, so this stays a measured claim.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="hosting">
  <h2>The hosted session</h2>
  <figure>
    <div class="fig">
      <svg viewBox="0 0 1040 400" role="img" aria-label="The browser talks to the local illuminate server over a WebSocket. The server runs the unmodified Claude Code binary as a child process using stream JSON, and Claude Code calls back through an MCP server to draw. A second, cheap Claude Code process does grounding. Both read the repo, and check re-reads it too.">
        <defs><marker id="fa2" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="currentColor"/></marker></defs>
        <rect class="fc" x="20" y="24" width="220" height="350" rx="12"/><text class="fh" x="36" y="48">Your browser</text>
        <rect class="fc" x="360" y="24" width="270" height="350" rx="12"/><text class="fh" x="376" y="48">illuminate server, 127.0.0.1, token</text>
        <rect class="fc" x="750" y="24" width="270" height="240" rx="12"/><text class="fh" x="766" y="48">Unmodified claude, your sign-in</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="40" y="64" width="180" height="60" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="130" y="90">Conversation</text><text class="fs" x="130" y="108">short replies, approvals</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="40" y="164" width="180" height="60" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="130" y="190">Canvas</text><text class="fs" x="130" y="208">React Flow, ELK, wireframes</text>
        <rect class="fb hi" x="380" y="64" width="230" height="60" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="495" y="90">Session manager (new)</text><text class="fs" x="495" y="108">one child process per conversation</text>
        <rect class="fb hi" x="380" y="154" width="230" height="60" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="495" y="180">Visual store + show tool (new)</text><text class="fs" x="495" y="198">parses sketches, saves to .illuminate/</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="380" y="244" width="230" height="50" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="495" y="274">check() and code facts</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="380" y="310" width="230" height="50" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="495" y="340">cliAgent (new) behind Agent</text>
        <rect class="fb" x="770" y="64" width="230" height="70" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="885" y="92">Main session</text><text class="fm" x="885" y="112">claude -p, stream-json</text>
        <rect class="fb ai" x="770" y="174" width="230" height="70" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="885" y="202">Grounder</text><text class="fm" x="885" y="222">claude -p --model haiku</text>
        <rect class="fb ok" x="770" y="304" width="230" height="60" rx="10"/><text class="ft" x="885" y="330">Your repo</text><text class="fs" x="885" y="348">edits only after approval</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M220,94 H380" marker-end="url(#fa2)" marker-start="url(#fa2)"/><text class="fl2" x="300" y="84">WebSocket</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M380,184 H220" marker-end="url(#fa2)"/><text class="fl2" x="300" y="174">visuals, statuses</text>

        <path class="fa" d="M610,335 C690,335 700,240 770,218" marker-end="url(#fa2)"/><text class="fl2" x="680" y="312">prompt, reply</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M610,269 C680,269 720,350 770,340" marker-end="url(#fa2)"/><text class="fl2" x="700" y="282">re-reads</text>
        <path class="fa" d="M980,244 V304" marker-end="url(#fa2)"/><text class="fl2" x="940" y="282">reads</text>
      </svg>
    </div>
    <figcaption>A message typed in the page goes straight to Claude Code's stdin, so hosting needs no channel. Tools, hooks and permission prompts all come through Claude Code's own flags. Existing maker, explainer and fix code keep working behind the <code>Agent</code> interface.</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table>
    <thead><tr><th style="width:20%">How it connects</th><th>Who it's for</th><th>Secret guard</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><b>Hosted</b> (the default)</td><td>Everyone with Claude Code: run <code>illume</code>, work in the page</td><td>Enforced, by hooks passed through <code>--settings</code></td><td>New. Depends on the terms question below</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>Channel</b></td><td>People who stay in their terminal</td><td>Instruction only</td><td>Built. Research preview, dev flag, failed to connect once in this session</td></tr>
      <tr><td><b>API key</b></td><td>Codex users, CI, anything without Claude Code</td><td>Enforced</td><td>Built (<code>sdkAgent</code>)</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table></div>
  <div class="callout">
    <p><b>The terms question decides the default, so settle it first.</b> Anthropic's <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance">legal page</a> says a third party can't offer claude.ai login or "collect, store, or intermediate" credentials. It also says each end user must authenticate with their own key or plan, and that nothing prevents them signing in to the unmodified binary with their own subscription.</p>
    <p>In this design illuminate never touches credentials and runs the unmodified binary on the user's machine. That looks allowed to me, and it's broader than what <code>HANDOFF.md</code> assumes, but it's my reading of the page. Ask Anthropic before a wider launch. If the answer is no, the same page works with an API key, and the channel stays as the free route.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="format">
  <h2>The format change</h2>
  <div class="two">
    <div>
      <h3>What Claude writes: the sketch language</h3>
      <pre class="code"><span class="c"># @ claims the code, + proposes, unmarked is a sketch</span>
view change "Why no welcome email, and the fix"
area app "The app"
area server "Server"
area auto "Automations"

box btn app entry "Mark as converted" <span class="a">@src/ui/PatientHeader.tsx#PatientHeader</span>
box mark server "Save and announce" <span class="a">@src/patients/service.ts#markConverted</span>
box rules auto "Run email rules" <span class="a">@src/automations/evaluate.ts#evaluateRules</span>
<span class="a">@</span>btn -> mark request "sends request"
<span class="x">mark -x rules "nothing listens" search "bus.on('patient.converted'" 0</span>
<span class="p">+box listen server "Conversion listener" touches src/server/routes.ts</span>
<span class="p">+mark -> listen "triggers"</span>
<span class="p">+listen -> rules "runs"</span></pre>
      <p style="margin:0;font-size:14px">The tool takes this as one string, and later calls send only changed lines, so the picture grows without being rewritten. An unmarked part can only ever look like a sketch, so forgetting a mark errs toward honesty.</p>
    </div>
    <div>
      <h3>What it becomes: <code>format.ts</code> version 2</h3>
      <pre class="code"><span class="c">// The one-way door: change deliberately, with tests.</span>
export const Claim = z.enum(['code', 'proposed', 'sketch']);
export const View = z.enum(['flow', 'journey', 'screen',
  'data', 'change', 'compare', 'build', 'sequence', 'state', 'sketch']);

Node = {
  ...today,
  claim: Claim.default('code'),  <span class="c">// v1 maps load unchanged</span>
  evidence: z.array(Evidence).default([]),  <span class="c">// parseMap: `code` needs it,
                                            // or a symbol facts can prove</span>
  touches: z.array(z.string()).optional(),  <span class="c">// `proposed`: checked</span>
}

Screen = {  <span class="c">// a node kind: a page and its rough wireframe</span>
  id, lane, route, claim, evidence,
  parts: [{ id, kind, label, at, evidence, wiresTo }],
}</pre>
      <p style="margin:0;font-size:14px">Statuses stay out of the format, as they are today. The report gains a count per claim. A proposed part whose code now exists and passes gets reported as built, which is what makes the build view work.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="rules">
  <h2>Rules in <code>CLAUDE.md</code> this changes</h2>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table>
    <thead><tr><th style="width:32%">Today</th><th style="width:36%">Becomes</th><th>Why it's safe</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>Nothing reaches the screen without passing <code>check()</code></td><td><b>Nothing looks true without passing <code>check()</code>.</b> Proposed and sketch parts appear at once, visibly marked.</td><td>The top bar counts them apart, and "matches the code" only ever counts checked parts.</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Claude never edits, <code>applyFix</code> writes the approved change</td><td><b>In a hosted session Claude Code edits,</b> each edit approved in the page through its permission prompt. <code>applyFix</code> stays for the other two connections.</td><td><code>HANDOFF.md</code> decision 5 already said a connected coding agent should make the edit. Still one editor at a time.</td></tr>
      <tr><td>All model calls go through one <code>Agent</code></td><td><b>Short jobs use <code>Agent</code>, and the conversation uses a new <code>Session</code>.</b></td><td>Tests inject scripted versions of both, and <code>npm test</code> still never calls a model.</td></tr>
      <tr><td>Read-only tools, secret guard enforced by <code>sdkAgent</code></td><td><b>The guard moves to hooks passed to every child process.</b></td><td>Stronger than the channel, where it's only an instruction.</td></tr>
      <tr><td>One checker, absences carry proof, map format is the one-way door, plain English, no model in facts or checker</td><td><b>Unchanged.</b></td><td>These are what stay hard to copy.</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table></div>
</section>

<section id="build">
  <h2>Build order</h2>
  <div class="prose"><p>Steps 1 to 3 are in sequence because everything sits on them. After that, steps 4 to 7 are independent and can run in parallel. Most of the work is small against today's code; steps 3 and 6 are the big ones.</p></div>
  <div class="tablewrap"><table>
    <thead><tr><th style="width:5%">Step</th><th style="width:26%">Build</th><th style="width:30%">Where</th><th>Done when</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">0</td><td><b>Spike and terms.</b> Ask Anthropic. Prove the child process on a subscription sign-in.</td><td>A throwaway script</td><td>One message, one MCP tool call and one permission prompt round-trip through a page</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">1</td><td><b>Format v2 and checker.</b> Claims, views, screens, per-claim report, built status.</td><td><code>core/src/format.ts</code>, <code>check.ts</code>, <code>edit.ts</code></td><td>All 9 saved maps load and recheck with the same results, new claim tests pass</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">2</td><td><b>Sketch language and <code>show</code>.</b> Parser, patches, facts pass. Works over the existing channel first.</td><td><code>core/src/sketch.ts</code>, <code>server/src/channel.ts</code></td><td>Claude draws on care-app, and named parts go solid with no model</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">3</td><td><b>Hosted session and the new app.</b> Conversation first, tabs of visuals, approvals, resume.</td><td><code>server/src/session.ts</code> (new), <code>server.ts</code>, <code>viewer/src/app.tsx</code>, <code>panel.tsx</code></td><td>A full session on care-app, from question to approved edit, without opening a terminal</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">4</td><td><b>Grounder.</b> <code>cliAgent</code>, model comparison, failure goes back to the main session.</td><td><code>server/src/agent.ts</code>, <code>prompts.ts</code></td><td>Haiku against Opus on care-app: confirmed count, time and cost written down</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">5</td><td><b>Change, compare, build.</b> Impact from facts, re-check as files change.</td><td><code>facts</code> call and import index, <code>server/src/impact.ts</code> (new), <code>viewer/src/graph.tsx</code></td><td>Care-app fix plays out for real: red arrow, two options, approved, turns solid</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">6</td><td><b>Screens.</b> Wireframe renderer, journey lanes, press-to-wire.</td><td><code>viewer/src/wireframe.tsx</code> (new), <code>layout.ts</code>, facts <code>page</code> entries, <code>journeys/fetches.ts</code></td><td>Dhruv's KPI question answered on a real dashboard</td></tr>
      <tr><td class="tag-t">7</td><td><b>Sequence, state, data views, export.</b></td><td><code>viewer/src/</code>, <code>server/src/store.ts</code></td><td>Each draws from a real question, and an exported page opens offline</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table></div>
</section>

<section id="hard">
  <h2>Where it will fight back</h2>
  <ul class="tight">
    <li><b>Wireframes can only be partly proven.</b> Facts know pages, components and fetch calls. They don't know what a page looks like. Claude writes the parts, and the checker verifies each label and wire against a cited line, so the arrangement stays marked as rough. Taste is out of scope.</li>
    <li><b>Solid means wired up, not working.</b> The build view can prove the listener exists and is connected. It can't prove the email arrives, and the wording has to say so every time.</li>
    <li><b>Knowing when to draw.</b> Too many pictures is as annoying as too few, and the model's judgment will drift. It needs the routing test from the start, and an easy "stop drawing" setting.</li>
    <li><b>Layouts that stay put.</b> Known boxes never move today, and that took work. Each new view needs the same guarantee when a patch arrives mid-conversation.</li>
    <li><b>Keeping a long session alive.</b> A child process per conversation means handling crashes, resume and two tabs. Long conversations also fill up, so tool replies must stay short.</li>
    <li><b>Claude could ship the generic version.</b> "Claude draws diagrams" is an obvious platform feature. The parts specific to illuminate are the checker, the proposed-to-solid loop and press-to-wire, so those should ship early and get shown first.</li>
  </ul>
</section>

<section id="decide">
  <h2>Decisions for you</h2>
  <ol class="tight">
    <li><b>Hosted as the default?</b> I recommend yes, if Anthropic's answer allows it.</li>
    <li><b>Retire the skill?</b> I recommend replacing it with <code>illume</code> opening the page, and keeping the channel for people who stay in their terminal.</li>
    <li><b>Who uses it first?</b> I recommend Dhruv, on a real client change. Dhruv's case needs press-to-wire, what-it-touches and approvals together, so it tests the whole idea.</li>
    <li><b>Update <code>CLAUDE.md</code> and <code>HANDOFF.md</code> before building?</b> I recommend yes, so every agent working on this follows the new rules from step 1.</li>
  </ol>
</section>

</main>

// ---------- renderer ----------
function resolve(sc, opts = {}) {
  const clone = (x) => ({ ...x });
  let nodes = sc.nodes.map(clone), edges = sc.edges.map(clone);
  if (sc.wires) {
    const w = sc.wires[opts.wire] || sc.wires[sc.defaultWire];
    nodes = nodes.concat(w.nodes.map(clone)); edges = edges.concat(w.edges.map(clone));
  }
  if (sc.stageApply) edges = sc.stageApply(opts.stage ?? 0, nodes, edges) || edges;
  return { nodes, edges };
}
function anchorOf(a, b, side) {
  const ax = a.x + a.w / 2, ay = a.y + a.h / 2, bx = b.x + b.w / 2, by = b.y + b.h / 2;
  const dx = bx - ax, dy = by - ay;
  const horiz = Math.abs(dx) * 0.8 > Math.abs(dy);
  if (horiz) return dx > 0 ? [a.x + a.w, ay, 1, 0, b.x, by, -1, 0] : [a.x, ay, -1, 0, b.x + b.w, by, 1, 0];
  return dy > 0 ? [ax, a.y + a.h, 0, 1, bx, b.y, 0, -1] : [ax, a.y, 0, -1, bx, b.y + b.h, 0, 1];
}
function draw(sc, opts = {}) {
  const mk = opts.prefix || 'm';
  const { nodes, edges } = resolve(sc, opts);
  const map = {};
  nodes.forEach((n) => {
    map[n.id] = n;
    (n.parts || []).forEach((p) => { if (p.id) map[p.id] = { x: n.x + p.x, y: n.y + p.y, w: p.w, h: p.h, name: p.label, ...p }; });
  });
  const live = !!opts.live;
  const attr = (id, label) => live ? ` data-id="${esc(id)}" tabindex="0" role="button" aria-label="${esc(label)}"` : '';
  const color = { ink: 'var(--line-strong)', ok: 'var(--ok)', dead: 'var(--dead)', ai: 'var(--ai)' };
  let s = '<defs>' + Object.entries(color).map(([k, c]) => `<marker id="${mk}-${k}" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" style="fill:${c}"/></marker>`).join('') + '</defs>';
  (sc.lanes || []).forEach((l) => {
    s += `<rect class="lane${l.alt ? ' alt' : ''}" x="8" y="${l.y}" width="944" height="${l.h}" rx="10"/>`;
    l.label.forEach((t, i) => { s += `<text class="lane-t" x="22" y="${l.y + 24 + i * 16}">${esc(t)}</text>`; });
  });
  (sc.areas || []).forEach((a) => { s += `<rect class="area" x="${a.x}" y="${a.y}" width="${a.w}" height="${a.h}" rx="14"/><text class="area-t" x="${a.x + 14}" y="${a.y + 23}">${esc(a.label)}</text>`; });
  if (sc.raw) s += sc.raw(mk);
  (sc.notes || []).forEach((t) => {
    s += `<rect class="note-box" x="${t.x}" y="${t.y}" width="${t.w}" height="62" rx="10"/><text class="note-t s" x="${t.x + 12}" y="${t.y + 25}">${esc(t.lines[0])}</text><text class="note-t" x="${t.x + 12}" y="${t.y + 46}">${esc(t.lines[1])}</text>`;
  });
  // arrows, under the boxes
  let labels = '';
  edges.forEach((e) => {
    const a = map[e.from], b = map[e.to];
    if (!a || !b) return;
    const [x1, y1, nx1, ny1, x2, y2, nx2, ny2] = anchorOf(a, b);
    const k = Math.max(26, Math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1) * 0.36);
    const c1 = [x1 + nx1 * k, y1 + ny1 * k], c2 = [x2 + nx2 * k, y2 + ny2 * k];
    const d = `M${x1},${y1} C${c1[0]},${c1[1]} ${c2[0]},${c2[1]} ${x2},${y2}`;
    const id = `${e.from}>${e.to}`;
    const m = e.claim === 'proposed' ? 'ok' : e.claim === 'missing' ? 'dead' : e.claim === 'checking' ? 'ai' : 'ink';
    const sel = opts.sel === id ? ' selected' : '';
    s += `<g class="e e-${e.claim}${sel}"${attr(id, `Arrow: ${e.label || 'connection'}`)}><path class="hit" d="${d}"/><path class="ln" d="${d}" marker-end="url(#${mk}-${m})"/></g>`;
    if (e.label) {
      const mx = e.lx ?? (x1 + 3 * c1[0] + 3 * c2[0] + x2) / 8, my = e.ly ?? (y1 + 3 * c1[1] + 3 * c2[1] + y2) / 8;
      const w = e.label.length * 6.2 + 10;
      labels += `<g class="e e-${e.claim}"><rect class="lbg" x="${mx - w / 2}" y="${my - 9}" width="${w}" height="17" rx="4"/><text class="lb" x="${mx}" y="${my + 4}">${esc(e.label)}</text></g>`;
    }
  });
  nodes.forEach((n) => {
    if (n.isScreen) {
      s += `<g class="n scr c-${n.claim}${opts.sel === n.id ? ' selected' : ''}"${attr(n.id, `Screen: ${n.title}`)}><rect class="halo" x="${n.x - 3}" y="${n.y - 3}" width="${n.w + 6}" height="${n.h + 6}" rx="15"/><rect class="scr-box" x="${n.x}" y="${n.y}" width="${n.w}" height="${n.h}" rx="12"/><text class="scr-t" x="${n.x + 14}" y="${n.y + 23}">${esc(n.title)}</text><text class="scr-r" x="${n.x + 14}" y="${n.y + 38}">${esc(n.route)}</text></g>`;
      n.parts.forEach((p) => {
        const px = n.x + p.x, py = n.y + p.y;
        const pa = p.id ? attr(p.id, `${p.label}: press to see what's behind it`) : '';
        const sel = p.id && (opts.sel === p.id || opts.wire === p.id) ? ' selected' : '';
        if (p.k === 'bar') s += `<rect class="w-bar" x="${px}" y="${py}" width="${p.w}" height="7" rx="3.5"/>`;
        if (p.k === 'tx') s += `<text class="w-tx" x="${px}" y="${py}">${esc(p.label)}</text>`;
        if (p.k === 'card') s += `<rect class="w-card" x="${px}" y="${py}" width="${p.w}" height="${p.h}" rx="9"/><text class="w-card-t" x="${px + 14}" y="${py + 22}">${esc(p.label)}</text>`;
        if (p.k === 'btn') s += `<g class="part w-btn${sel}"${pa}><rect x="${px}" y="${py}" width="${p.w}" height="${p.h}" rx="7"/><text x="${px + p.w / 2}" y="${py + p.h / 2 + 4}">${esc(p.label)}</text></g>`;
        if (p.k === 'tag') s += `<g class="part w-tag${sel}"${pa}><rect x="${px}" y="${py}" width="${p.w}" height="${p.h}" rx="${p.h / 2}"/><text x="${px + p.w / 2}" y="${py + p.h / 2 + 4}">${esc(p.label)}</text></g>`;
        if (p.k === 'kpi') s += `<g class="part w-kpi${sel}"${pa}><rect x="${px}" y="${py}" width="${p.w}" height="${p.h}" rx="9"/><text class="v" x="${px + 16}" y="${py + 56}">${esc(p.value)}</text><text class="l" x="${px + 16}" y="${py + 84}">${esc(p.label)}</text></g>`;
      });
      return;
    }
    const cls = `n c-${n.claim} k-${n.kind}${n.touches ? ' touched' : ''}${opts.sel === n.id ? ' selected' : ''}`;
    s += `<g class="${cls}"${attr(n.id, `${n.name}. ${n.claim === 'code' ? 'In the code' : n.claim}`)}>`
      + `<rect class="halo" x="${n.x - 3}" y="${n.y - 3}" width="${n.w + 6}" height="${n.h + 6}" rx="16"/>`
      + `<rect class="box" x="${n.x}" y="${n.y}" width="${n.w}" height="${n.h}" rx="13"/>`
      + `<text class="hd" x="${n.x + 12}" y="${n.y + 19}">${KIND[n.kind] || ''}</text><text class="fl" x="${n.x + n.w - 11}" y="${n.y + 19}">${FLAG[n.claim]}</text>`
      + `<text class="nm" x="${n.x + 12}" y="${n.y + 40}">${esc(n.name)}</text><text class="sb" x="${n.x + 12}" y="${n.y + 58}">${esc(n.sub || '')}</text></g>`;
  });
  return `<svg viewBox="0 0 960 540" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" ${live ? '' : `role="img" aria-label="${esc(sc.title)}"`}>${s}${labels}</svg>`;
}
function trustOf(sc, opts) {
  const { nodes, edges } = resolve(sc, opts);
  const c = { code: 0, proposed: 0, sketch: 0, missing: 0, checking: 0 };
  [...nodes, ...edges].forEach((x) => { if (x.claim in c) c[x.claim]++; else if (x.claim === 'behind') c.code++; });
  const bits = [];
  if (c.code) bits.push(`<span class="t-code">✓ ${c.code} match the code</span>`);
  if (c.checking) bits.push(`<span class="t-checking">${c.checking} being checked</span>`);
  if (c.proposed) bits.push(`<span class="t-proposed">+ ${c.proposed} proposed</span>`);
  if (c.sketch) bits.push(`<span class="t-sketch">${c.sketch} sketched</span>`);
  if (c.missing) bits.push(`<span class="t-missing">✕ ${c.missing} missing</span>`);
  return bits.join('');
}

// ---------- the scripted session ----------
const TURNS = [
  { scene: 'flow', you: 'Why doesn’t a patient get a welcome email after they’re converted?', claude: 'The conversion gets announced, but nothing listens for the announcement, so the email rules never run. The red arrow is the break.' },
  { scene: 'journey', you: 'Show me this from the front desk’s side.', claude: 'Staff see the welcome email marked Active, so they’d expect it to send. The dotted line shows what their press actually sets off.' },
  { scene: 'screen', you: 'Where does the outbox count come from?', claude: 'It counts what gets sent, and it stays at 0 because the rules that queue email never run. Press the other controls to see their wiring.' },
  { scene: 'compare', you: 'How would we fix it? Show me the options.', claude: 'Two ways. I’d take A: three lines in one file, and the announcement finally gets used. Both give the email rules a second caller, so starting the nightly job later could send two emails.' },
  { scene: 'build', you: 'Build option A.', claude: 'Here’s the edit. It stays dashed until you approve it and the code passes the check.', approve: true },
];
const BUILD_FEED = ['Editing src/server/routes.ts', 'Rechecking 16 parts against the code', 'The listener is in the code and connected'];
const log = document.getElementById('log'), canvas = document.getElementById('canvas'), trust = document.getElementById('trust'),
  tabs = document.getElementById('tabs'), vtitle = document.getElementById('vtitle'), detail = document.getElementById('detail'), q = document.getElementById('q');
const st = { turn: 0, shown: 0, scene: 'flow', sel: null, wire: 'w-outbox', stage: 0, approved: false, extra: [] };
let timers = [];
const stopTimers = () => { timers.forEach(clearTimeout); timers = []; };

function renderLog() {
  let h = '';
  TURNS.slice(0, st.shown + 1).forEach((t, i) => {
    h += `<div class="m-you">${esc(t.you)}</div><div class="m-claude"><p>${esc(t.claude)}</p><button type="button" class="vis-chip${st.scene === t.scene ? ' on' : ''}" data-open="${i}">${esc(SCENES[t.scene].tab)}</button>`;
    if (t.approve) {
      if (!st.approved) h += `<div class="approve"><b>Allow this edit to src/server/routes.ts?</b><pre>+ import { bus } from '../events/bus';
+ import { evaluateRules } from '../automations/evaluate';
+ bus.on('patient.converted', evaluateRules);</pre><div class="row"><button type="button" class="btn" id="allow">Allow</button><span style="font-size:12.5px;color:var(--muted)">Claude Code’s own prompt, shown here</span></div></div>`;
      else {
        BUILD_FEED.slice(0, st.stage + 1).forEach((f, j) => { if (j < st.stage || st.stage < 2) h += `<div class="work">${esc(f)}</div>`; });
        if (st.stage === 2) h += `<div class="work">${esc(BUILD_FEED[2])}</div><p>Done. The red arrow is gone. That proves the wiring exists, so run the app to see the email arrive.</p>`;
      }
    }
    h += '</div>';
  });
  st.extra.forEach((x) => { h += `<div class="m-you">${esc(x.you)}</div><div class="m-claude"><p>${esc(x.claude)}</p></div>`; });
  log.innerHTML = h;
  log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight;
  const allow = document.getElementById('allow');
  if (allow) allow.onclick = runBuild;
}
function renderCanvas() {
  const sc = SCENES[st.scene];
  canvas.innerHTML = draw(sc, { live: true, sel: st.sel, wire: st.wire, stage: st.scene === 'build' ? st.stage : undefined, prefix: 'live' });
  vtitle.textContent = sc.title;
  trust.innerHTML = trustOf(sc, { wire: st.wire, stage: st.scene === 'build' ? st.stage : undefined });
  tabs.innerHTML = TURNS.map((t, i) => `<button type="button" class="tab" data-open="${i}" aria-pressed="${st.scene === t.scene}"${i > st.shown ? ' style="opacity:.55"' : ''}><span class="n">${i + 1}</span>${esc(SCENES[t.scene].tab)}</button>`).join('');
}
function renderDetail() {
  const sc = SCENES[st.scene];
  if (!st.sel) { detail.hidden = true; return; }
  const { nodes, edges } = resolve(sc, { wire: st.wire, stage: st.scene === 'build' ? st.stage : undefined });
  let item = nodes.find((n) => n.id === st.sel);
  if (!item) nodes.forEach((n) => (n.parts || []).forEach((p) => { if (p.id === st.sel) item = { name: p.label, ...p }; }));
  if (!item) { const e = edges.find((x) => `${x.from}>${x.to}` === st.sel); if (e) item = { name: e.label || 'Connection', ...e }; }
  if (!item) { detail.hidden = true; return; }
  const status = { code: 'In the code', proposed: 'Proposed', sketch: 'Sketch', missing: 'Missing', checking: 'Being checked', behind: 'In the code' }[item.claim] || 'In the code';
  detail.hidden = false;
  detail.innerHTML = `<b>${esc(item.name)}</b><span>${esc(status)}${item.say ? '. ' + esc(item.say) : '.'}</span>${item.cite ? `<span class="cite">${esc(item.cite)}</span>` : ''}`;
}
function setComposer() {
  const next = TURNS[st.shown + 1];
  if (st.sel) { q.value = ''; q.placeholder = 'Ask about what you selected…'; }
  else if (next) { q.value = next.you; q.placeholder = ''; }
  else { q.value = ''; q.placeholder = 'Ask about anything on the canvas…'; }
}
function open(i, advance) {
  stopTimers();
  const t = TURNS[i];
  if (advance || i > st.shown) st.shown = Math.max(st.shown, i);
  st.scene = t.scene; st.sel = null;
  if (t.scene === 'build' && !st.approved) st.stage = 0;
  renderLog(); renderCanvas(); renderDetail(); setComposer();
}
function runBuild() {
  st.approved = true;
  const instant = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  const go = (stage) => { st.stage = stage; renderLog(); renderCanvas(); renderDetail(); };
  if (instant) return go(2);
  go(0);
  timers.push(setTimeout(() => go(1), 900));
  timers.push(setTimeout(() => go(2), 2800));
}
document.getElementById('app').addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const o = e.target.closest('[data-open]');
  if (o) return open(+o.dataset.open);
  const t = e.target.closest('[data-id]');
  if (!t || !canvas.contains(t)) return;
  const id = t.dataset.id;
  if (SCENES[st.scene].wires && SCENES[st.scene].wires[id]) st.wire = id;
  st.sel = id; renderCanvas(); renderDetail(); setComposer();
  const again = canvas.querySelector(`[data-id="${CSS.escape(id)}"]`);
  if (again) again.focus({ preventScroll: true });
});
canvas.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key !== 'Enter' && e.key !== ' ') return;
  const t = e.target.closest('[data-id]');
  if (t) { e.preventDefault(); t.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true })); }
});
document.getElementById('composer').addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const v = q.value.trim();
  const next = TURNS[st.shown + 1];
  if (next && v === next.you) return open(st.shown + 1, true);
  if (!v) return;
  st.extra.push({ you: v, claude: st.sel ? 'In the real app Claude answers here, about what you selected, and can add to the picture. This prototype is scripted.' : 'In the real app Claude answers here, drawing if it helps. This prototype is scripted, so clear the box or press a tab to carry on.' });
  q.value = ''; renderLog();
});

// ---------- gallery ----------
const GALLERY = [
  ['flow', 'Flow map', 'How something works across files. Today’s map.', 'Every box and arrow against code facts and cited lines. Absences by their search.'],
  ['journey', 'Journey', 'What a person does and sees, by role, with the backend beneath.', 'Routes, pages and fetch calls. The dotted link from a press to its request.'],
  ['screen', 'Wired screen', '“Where does this number come from?” Press a control to see its wiring.', 'Each label against its line, and each wire as a normal arrow. The arrangement is rough.'],
```

```text
// The one place illuminate talks to a model: a read-only Claude Agent SDK session that returns structured output.
// Read, Grep and Glob only; secret files are refused and left out of searches. Tests swap in a fake `Agent`.
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { query, type HookCallback, type PreToolUseHookInput } from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk';
import { isSecretPath } from '@illuminate/core';

export type Progress = { kind: 'read' | 'search' | 'list' | 'status'; text: string };

export type AgentRequest = {
  prompt: string;
  /** What this is for, in a few plain words ("Making the map for …"). Shown when the request is handed to Claude Code. */
  label?: string;
  schema: Record<string, unknown>;
  cwd: string;
  /** Continue an earlier session (follow-up questions keep what was already read). */
  resume?: string | null;
  model?: string;
  maxTurns?: number;
  /** Tools Claude may use: a subset of Read, Grep and Glob (default all three; `[]` for none, answering from the prompt). */
  tools?: readonly string[];
  onProgress?: (p: Progress) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
};
export type AgentResponse = { output: unknown; sessionId: string | null; cost: number | null };
export type Agent = (req: AgentRequest) => Promise<AgentResponse>;

export const DEFAULT_MODEL = process.env.ILLUMINATE_MODEL ?? 'claude-opus-5-5';
const READ_ONLY = ['Read', 'Grep', 'Glob'];
/** ripgrep glob that leaves secret files out of a search the model didn't scope itself. */
const NOT_SECRETS = '!**/{.env,.env.*,*.pem,*.key,*.p12,id_rsa*,id_ed25519*,.npmrc,.netrc}';

/** A plain-English progress line for a tool call, with paths relative to the repo. */
export function progressOf(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd: string): Progress | null {
  const rel = (p: unknown) => (typeof p === 'string' ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, p)) || '.' : '');
  if (name === 'Read') return { kind: 'read', text: `Reading ${rel(input.file_path)}` };
  if (name === 'Grep') return { kind: 'search', text: `Searching for "${String(input.pattern ?? '')}"${input.path ? ` in ${rel(input.path)}` : ''}` };
  if (name === 'Glob') return { kind: 'list', text: `Looking for files matching ${String(input.pattern ?? '')}` };
  return null;
}

/** Refuse secret files, and keep repo-wide searches away from them. */
export function secretGuard(cwd: string): HookCallback {
  return async (input) => {
    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
    const ti = (i.tool_input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    const target = typeof ti.file_path === 'string' ? ti.file_path : typeof ti.path === 'string' ? ti.path : null;
    const rel = target ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, target)) : null;
    if (rel && (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel))) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Only files inside this repo can be read.' } };
    }
    if (rel && isSecretPath(rel)) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Secret files are never read.' } };
    }
    if (i.tool_name === 'Grep' && ti.glob === undefined && ti.type === undefined) {
      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'allow', updatedInput: { ...ti, glob: NOT_SECRETS } } };
    }
    return {};
  };
}

export const sdkAgent: Agent = async (req) => {
  const abortController = new AbortController();
  req.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => abortController.abort(), { once: true });
  // Never more than read-only, whatever the caller asks for.
  const tools = READ_ONLY.filter((t) => (req.tools ?? READ_ONLY).includes(t));
  const q = query({
    prompt: req.prompt,
    options: {
      cwd: req.cwd,
      model: req.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL,
      tools,
      allowedTools: tools,
      permissionMode: 'dontAsk',
      settingSources: [],
      strictMcpConfig: true,
      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: req.schema },
      maxTurns: req.maxTurns ?? 60,
      abortController,
      hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: 'Read|Grep|Glob', hooks: [secretGuard(req.cwd)] }] },
      ...(req.resume ? { resume: req.resume } : {}),
    },
  });
  let sessionId: string | null = null;
  for await (const m of q) {
    if ('session_id' in m && typeof m.session_id === 'string') sessionId = m.session_id;
    if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
      for (const block of m.message.content) {
        if (block.type !== 'tool_use') continue;
        const p = progressOf(block.name, (block.input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>, req.cwd);
        if (p) req.onProgress?.(p);
      }
    }
    if (m.type === 'result') {
      if (m.subtype !== 'success' || m.structured_output === undefined) {
        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Claude stopped before answering (${m.subtype}).`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
      }
      return { output: m.structured_output, sessionId, cost: m.total_cost_usd };
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Claude returned no result.');
};

function selectionLines(map: CodeMap, s: Selection): SelectionLine[] {
  const nodes = new Map(map.nodes.map((n) => [n.id, n]));
  const label = (id: string) => nodes.get(id)?.name ?? id;
  return [
    ...(s.nodes ?? []).filter((id) => nodes.has(id)).map((id) => ({ id, label: `box "${label(id)}"` })),
    ...(s.edges ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
      const e = map.edges.find((x) => x.id === id);
      return e ? [{ id, label: `arrow "${e.label}" from "${label(e.from)}" to "${label(e.to)}"` }] : [];
    }),
    ...(s.absences ?? []).flatMap((id) => {
      const a = map.absences.find((x) => x.id === id);
      return a ? [{ id, label: `missing connection: ${a.claim}` }] : [];
    }),
  ];
}

function statusOf(report: CheckReport, id: string): RefStatus['status'] {
  const c = report.nodes[id] ?? report.edges[id] ?? report.absences[id];
  return c ? c.status : 'unknown';
}

export async function answer(o: AnswerOptions): Promise<{ answer: Answer; map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport; sessionId: string | null }> {
  const before = check(o.map, o.root);
  const selection = selectionLines(o.map, o.selection);
  const status = (text: string) => o.onProgress?.({ kind: 'status', text });
  const live0 = mapIds(o.map);
  const selected = (o.selection.nodes?.length ?? 0) + (o.selection.edges?.length ?? 0) + (o.selection.absences?.length ?? 0) > 0;
  let cost = 0;
  let missing = '';

  if (o.quick !== false && !o.wordsOnly) {
    status('Answering from the map');
    try {
      const res = await o.agent({
        prompt: quickAnswerPrompt(o.map, before, selection, o.question, citedExcerpts(o.root, o.map, o.selection), o.earlier ?? [], o.otherMaps ?? []),
        label: `Answering "${o.question}" from the map`,
        schema: QUICK_ANSWER_SCHEMA,
        cwd: o.root,
        tools: [],
        resume: null,
        model: o.model,
        maxTurns: 3,
        signal: o.signal,
      });
      cost += res.cost ?? 0;
      const quick = RawQuickAnswer.safeParse(res.output);
      // Something selected on this map means the question is about this map, whatever the first try thought.
      if (quick.success && quick.data.route === 'elsewhere' && !selected) {
        const existing = (o.otherMaps ?? []).find((m) => m.id === quick.data.existingMap) ?? null;
        const result: Answer = {
          id: `ans-${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}`,
          question: o.question,
          selection: o.selection,
          concept: '',
          refs: [],
          moves: { focus: null, highlight: [] },
          added: [],
          problems: [],
          fix: null,
          source: 'map',
          offer: { question: quick.data.newQuestion.trim() || o.question, existing, status: 'pending', mapId: null },
          cost,
        };
        return { answer: result, map: o.map, report: before, sessionId: o.session };
      }
      if (quick.success && quick.data.route === 'answer' && quick.data.concept.trim()) {
        const q = quick.data;
        const result: Answer = {
          id: `ans-${crypto.randomBytes(4).toString('hex')}`,
          question: o.question,
          selection: o.selection,
          concept: q.concept,
          refs: [...new Set(q.refs)].map((id) => ({ id, status: statusOf(before, id) })),
          moves: {
            focus: q.moves?.focus && live0.has(q.moves.focus) ? q.moves.focus : null,
            highlight: (q.moves?.highlight ?? []).filter((id) => live0.has(id)),
          },
          added: [],
          problems: [],
          fix: null,
          source: 'map',
          offer: null,
          cost,
        };
        // The map didn't change, and the explainer session (what Claude has read in the code) carries on as it was.
        return { answer: result, map: o.map, report: before, sessionId: o.session };
      }
      if (quick.success) missing = quick.data.missing;
    } catch (err) {
      if (o.signal?.aborted) throw err;
      // A failed quick try isn't the end: Claude with the code still gets the question.
      cost += (err as { cost?: number }).cost ?? 0;
    }
    status('Looking in the code');
  }

  const res = await o.agent({
    prompt: explainerPrompt(o.map, before, selection, o.question, missing, o.wordsOnly, o.earlier ?? []),
    label: `Answering "${o.question}" from the code`,
    schema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,
```

```text
// illuminate as a Claude Code channel: an MCP server Claude Code starts over stdio, so the person's own Claude Code
// session does the reading and writing (on their own sign-in) instead of a separate Agent SDK session with its own key.
//
// The local illuminate server runs inside this process with a bridge `Agent` (bridge.ts). Work reaches Claude two ways:
// - in tool results: `illuminate_map` and `illuminate_submit` wait briefly for the next request, so making a map
//   (draft, check, repair) runs within one turn;
// - as a channel message, when work starts from the browser (a question on the map, New map) and no tool call is
//   waiting. Claude then calls `illuminate_next`.
// Only the person's browser can start work, and the page needs illuminate's token, so the channel is gated.
// Channels are a Claude Code research preview: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js';
import { StdioServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js';
import { CallToolRequestSchema, ListToolsRequestSchema, type ServerNotification } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js';
import { createBridge, type Bridge, type BridgeRequest } from './bridge';
import { openBrowser } from './browser';
import { startServer, type IlluminateServer, type ServerEvent } from './server';
import { createStore } from './store';

export type ChannelOptions = {
  /** The repo maps are about unless a tool call names another (Claude Code passes CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). */
  root: string;
  /** How a link is opened in the browser (tests pass a no-op). */
  open?: (url: string) => void;
  /** How long a tool call waits for the next piece of work before handing the turn back (default 90 s). */
  waitMs?: number;
  /** Port for the local server (default 4317, or the next free one). */
  port?: number;
};

export const CHANNEL_INSTRUCTIONS = [
  'illuminate draws checked, interactive maps of how this codebase works, in the person\'s browser. You do the reading and writing; illuminate checks every claim against the code before it shows anything.',
  '- When the person asks how something works across files ("what happens when…", "how does X reach Y") or asks for a map, diagram or walkthrough, call illuminate_map with their question in their own words.',
  '- illuminate gives you work as requests, in tool results or announced by a <channel source="illuminate" request_id="..."> message (call illuminate_next to get it). Each request says what to do and the JSON to return. Explore the code with Read, Grep and Glob, then call illuminate_submit with the request_id and your output. If the result holds another request, do that one too. If you can\'t finish one, call illuminate_fail.',
  '- While working on an illuminate request, don\'t edit files or run commands that change anything, and never read secret files (.env, keys). A fix is only proposed; illuminate applies it after the person approves it on the map.',
  '- Answers are shown on the map. In the terminal, say at most a sentence or two.',
].join('\n');

const TOOLS = [
  {
    name: 'illuminate_map',
    description: 'Make a checked map that answers a question about how this codebase works, and open it in the person\'s browser. Returns the first piece of work for you to do.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        question: { type: 'string', description: 'The person\'s question, in their own words.' },
        repo: { type: 'string', description: 'The repo root, if not the project Claude Code was started in.' },
      },
      required: ['question'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_next',
    description: 'Get the next piece of work illuminate has for you (after an illuminate channel message).',
    inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {} },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_submit',
    description: 'Hand in your output for an illuminate request. It is checked; if it can\'t be read you get the problems back to fix. Returns the next piece of work, if there is one.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        request_id: { type: 'string' },
        output: { type: 'object', description: 'JSON matching the request\'s schema.' },
      },
      required: ['request_id', 'output'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_fail',
    description: 'Give up on an illuminate request, saying why in plain words. The person sees it on the map.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { request_id: { type: 'string' }, reason: { type: 'string' } },
      required: ['request_id', 'reason'],
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'illuminate_open',
    description: 'Open saved maps in the person\'s browser: one map, or the list of all of them. Returns the maps saved in the repo.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        map_id: { type: 'string', description: 'A saved map\'s id; leave out for the list.' },
        repo: { type: 'string' },
      },
    },
  },
] as const;

/** A request as Claude reads it: what it's for, how to answer, the prompt, and the output schema. */
export function requestText(r: BridgeRequest): string {
  return [
    `## illuminate request ${r.id}: ${r.label}`,
    '',
    `When you're done, call illuminate_submit with request_id "${r.id}" and \`output\`: a JSON object matching the schema at the end. Don't edit any files.`,
    r.tools.length ? '' : 'Answer from what is in this request alone. Don\'t read the code for this one.',
    r.continues ? 'This follows on from your earlier work for illuminate in this conversation.' : '',
    '',
    '---',
    r.prompt,
    '---',
    '',
    '## Output schema (JSON Schema)',
    JSON.stringify(r.schema),
  ].filter((line, i, all) => line !== '' || all[i - 1] !== '').join('\n');
}

type Text = { content: { type: 'text'; text: string }[]; isError?: boolean };
const text = (t: string, isError = false): Text => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: t }], ...(isError ? { isError } : {}) });

export function createChannel(o: ChannelOptions) {
  const open = o.open ?? openBrowser;
  const waitMs = o.waitMs ?? 90_000;
  const servers = new Map<string, Promise<IlluminateServer>>();
  /** Listeners for "something finished", so a waiting tool call can say so. */
  const finished = new Set<(message: string) => void>();
  const lastReport = new Map<string, { confirmed: number; claims: number }>();

  const mcp = new Server(
    { name: 'illuminate', version: '0.1.0' },
    { capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} }, tools: {} }, instructions: CHANNEL_INSTRUCTIONS },
  );

  const bridge: Bridge = createBridge({
    announce: (r) => {
      void mcp
        .notification({
          method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
          params: { content: `illuminate has work for you: ${r.label}. Call illuminate_next to get it.`, meta: { request_id: r.id } },
        } as unknown as ServerNotification)
        .catch(() => {});
    },
  });

  const rootOf = (repo: unknown): string => {
    const dir = path.resolve(o.root, typeof repo === 'string' && repo.trim() ? repo : '.');
    if (!fs.existsSync(dir) || !fs.statSync(dir).isDirectory()) throw new Error(`No such folder: ${dir}`);
    return fs.realpathSync(dir);
  };

  const serverFor = (root: string): Promise<IlluminateServer> => {
    let s = servers.get(root);
    if (!s) {
      s = startServer({
        root,
        port: o.port ?? 4317,
        agent: bridge.agent,
        // The Stop button stops the page's server; the next illuminate tool call starts a new one.
        onStop: () => servers.delete(root),
        onEvent: (e) => void onEvent(root, e),
      });
      s.catch(() => servers.delete(root));
      servers.set(root, s);
    }
    return s;
  };

  async function onEvent(root: string, e: ServerEvent) {
    if (e.type === 'map') lastReport.set(e.mapId, { confirmed: e.report.summary.confirmed, claims: e.report.summary.claims });
    if (e.type !== 'job' || e.status === 'started') return;
    let message: string;
    if (e.status === 'failed') message = `illuminate couldn't finish "${e.question}": ${e.error ?? 'unknown error'}`;
    else if (e.job === 'make') {
      const s = await servers.get(root);
      const r = lastReport.get(e.mapId);
      message = [
        `The map for "${e.question}" is ready${r ? `: ${r.confirmed} of ${r.claims} claims confirmed against the code` : ''}.`,
        s ? `It's open in the browser: ${s.pageUrl(e.mapId)}` : '',
        'Tell the person in a sentence; the map does the explaining. They can take the walkthrough, or select any box and ask about it there.',
      ].filter(Boolean).join('\n');
    } else message = `The answer to "${e.question}" is shown on the map.`;
    for (const f of [...finished]) f(message);
  }

  /** After handing something in: the next request, or what finished, or (after a while) that nothing is needed yet. */
  async function whatNext(): Promise<Text> {
    const ac = new AbortController();
    let onFinish: ((m: string) => void) | null = null;
    const done = new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
      onFinish = resolve;
      finished.add(resolve);
    });
    const timer = new Promise<null>((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve(null), waitMs).unref?.());
    try {
      const winner = await Promise.race([
        bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal).then((r) => (r ? { request: r } : null)),
        done.then((message) => ({ message })),
        timer,
      ]);
      if (winner && 'request' in winner) return text(requestText(winner.request));
      if (winner && 'message' in winner) return text(winner.message);
      return text('illuminate is still working on its side. If it needs you, an illuminate channel message will say so.');
    } finally {
      ac.abort();
      if (onFinish) finished.delete(onFinish);
    }
  }

  mcp.setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, async () => ({ tools: TOOLS.map((t) => ({ ...t })) as never }));

  mcp.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, async (req): Promise<Text> => {
    const args = (req.params.arguments ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
    try {
      switch (req.params.name) {
        case 'illuminate_map': {
          const question = String(args.question ?? '').trim();
          if (!question) return text('Pass the person\'s question.', true);
          const server = await serverFor(rootOf(args.repo));
          const id = server.startMap(question);
          // The job runs asynchronously, so listening now misses neither the first request nor an early failure.
          const next = whatNext();
          const url = server.pageUrl(id);
          open(url);
          const first = await next;
          return { ...first, content: [{ type: 'text', text: `The map is opening in the browser: ${url}\nTell the person, and give them the link in case the tab didn't appear.\n` }, ...first.content] };
        }
        case 'illuminate_next': {
          const r = bridge.next();
          return text(r ? requestText(r) : 'Nothing is waiting right now.');
        }
        case 'illuminate_submit': {
          const id = String(args.request_id ?? '');
          // What follows (a repair round, the check's result) only happens once this handler yields to the event loop,
          // so listening right after submitting misses nothing.
          const r = bridge.submit(id, args.output);
          if (r.ok) return await whatNext();
          return text(`That output for ${id} can't be used yet. Fix these and call illuminate_submit again:\n${r.problems.map((p) => `- ${p}`).join('\n')}`, true);
        }
        case 'illuminate_fail': {
          const ok = bridge.fail(String(args.request_id ?? ''), String(args.reason ?? 'no reason given'));
          return text(ok ? 'Told the person on the map.' : 'No such request is waiting.');
        }
        case 'illuminate_open': {
          const root = rootOf(args.repo);
          const server = await serverFor(root);
          const mapId = typeof args.map_id === 'string' && args.map_id ? args.map_id : undefined;
          const url = server.pageUrl(mapId);
          open(url);
          const maps = createStore(root).list();
          return text([`Opened ${url}`, '', maps.length ? 'Saved maps:' : 'No maps saved in this repo yet.', ...maps.map((m) => `${m.id}  ${m.question}`)].join('\n'));
        }
        default:
          return text(`Unknown tool: ${req.params.name}`, true);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      return text(err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err), true);
    }
  });

  return {
    mcp,
    bridge,
    async close() {
      for (const s of servers.values()) await s.then((x) => x.close()).catch(() => {});
      servers.clear();
      await mcp.close();
    },
  };
}

/** `illume channel`: serve the channel over stdio until Claude Code closes it. stdout belongs to MCP, so logs go to stderr. */
export async function runChannel(o: Omit<ChannelOptions, 'root'> & { root?: string }) {
  console.log = console.error;
  console.info = console.error;
  const channel = createChannel({ ...o, root: o.root ?? process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR ?? process.cwd() });
  let stopping = false;
  const stop = () => {
    if (stopping) return;
    stopping = true;
    void channel.close().finally(() => process.exit(0));
  };
  channel.mcp.onclose = stop;
  process.on('SIGINT', stop);
  process.on('SIGTERM', stop);
  await channel.mcp.connect(new StdioServerTransport());
}
```

```text
// illuminate as a Claude Code channel, driven the way Claude Code drives it: an MCP client calls the tools, and the
// test plays Claude by submitting output. No model is called.
import { Client } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js';
import { InMemoryTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/inMemory.js';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createBridge } from '../src/bridge';
import { createChannel } from '../src/channel';
import { MAP_SCHEMA } from '../src/schemas';
import { CARE_MAP, cleanup, copyCareApp, waitFor } from './helpers';

describe('the bridge', () => {
  it('announces a request when nothing is waiting, and hands back output once it reads', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const reply = bridge.agent({ prompt: 'Draw it', label: 'Making a map', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/' });
    expect(announced).toEqual(['r1']);
    expect(bridge.next()).toMatchObject({ id: 'r1', label: 'Making a map', continues: false });

    const bad = bridge.submit('r1', { version: 1 });
    expect(bad.ok).toBe(false);
    expect(bridge.submit('r1', JSON.stringify(CARE_MAP))).toEqual({ ok: true });
    await expect(reply).resolves.toMatchObject({ output: CARE_MAP, sessionId: 'claude-code', cost: null });
    expect(bridge.outstanding()).toEqual([]);
    expect(bridge.submit('r1', CARE_MAP).ok).toBe(false);
  });

  it('hands a request to a waiting tool call instead of announcing it, and lets Claude give up', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const waiting = bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal);
    const reply = bridge.agent({ prompt: 'Answer', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/', tools: [], resume: 'claude-code' });
    await expect(waiting).resolves.toMatchObject({ id: 'r1', tools: [], continues: true });
    expect(announced).toEqual([]);
    expect(bridge.fail('r1', 'the code is not there')).toBe(true);
    await expect(reply).rejects.toThrow('the code is not there');
  });

  it('drops a waiting tool call once it stops listening', async () => {
    const announced: string[] = [];
    const bridge = createBridge({ announce: (r) => announced.push(r.id) });
    const ac = new AbortController();
    const waiting = bridge.waitForNext(ac.signal);
    ac.abort();
    await expect(waiting).resolves.toBeNull();
    void bridge.agent({ prompt: 'x', schema: MAP_SCHEMA, cwd: '/' }).catch(() => {});
    expect(announced).toEqual(['r1']);
  });
});
```

This was a bug in illuminate, not a network problem. The question reached nobody, and illuminate had no limit on how long it would wait, so the page looked busy forever.

**What happened:**
- A question asked on the map is sent into your Claude Code session as a channel message. That only works if the session was started with `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:illuminate`.
- You have six Claude Code sessions open in the hallucinated repo, and none of them was started that way. So the message was silently dropped, and nothing told the page.
- Neither saved map there (the shirt-generation one and "how does my generation process work in the code") has any answers recorded, which matches a question that never got through.

**What I changed:**
- **`packages/server/src/bridge.ts`:** the page now shows "Waiting for Claude Code to pick this up" instead of claiming Claude is working. If nothing picks the question up within 30 seconds, it explains why and what to do. After 5 minutes it gives up with an error. Once Claude has picked a question up, there's no time limit.
- **`packages/server/src/explainer.ts`:** when nobody picked up the first attempt, it doesn't start a second one that would wait just as long.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** added a note about this under Channel.
- Two new tests. All 49 server tests and the typecheck pass. I haven't tried the fix against a real Claude Code session.

**To get going again:** the sessions you have open still run the old code. Close the ones in the hallucinated repo and start one with `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:illuminate`. As a stopgap, in any open session you can ask Claude to "check illuminate for work", which fetches the waiting question directly.

**A second problem I didn't fix:** each of those six sessions runs its own illuminate server. Port 4317 belongs to a `claude --resume` session from four days ago. So a map page sends its questions to whichever session started that page's server, which may not be the terminal you're watching. The simplest fix is to have a new channel take over an existing server for the same repo, or refuse to start a second one. Say if you want that done.
